name: Pinky Purple
lede: Pinky Purple is a casual modifier name for a vivid magenta-leaning purple; the only book note is that the word heather now means exactly this.

sections.title: A modifier name
sections.body: The name is plain grammar, pinky plus purple [2]. It enters our sources with the xkcd survey of 2010, and Wikipedia lists it among Crayola names [2]. ISCC-NBS would call the swatch a strong reddish purple, though the match is loose [2]. Its parent is [[purple]], and it is a neighbor of [[rose-purple]] and [[magenta]] [2]. Wikipedia ties the name to a Crayola color, so it may be a crayon name before it was a survey answer, though our sources give no date for that [2].

sections.title: Heather, pinky purple
sections.body: St Clair's glossary of color words defines [[heather]] as a pre-twentieth-century synonym for mottled that now means pinky purple [1]. So the plant name has become a color word that books gloss with this exact phrase [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our archive has this color covering at least 1% of its canvas, as photographed [3]. That describes this archive, not painting as a whole [3].

disambiguation.gloss: a greyer, softer purple-pink, named for the plant

questions.q: What did heather mean before the twentieth century, per St Clair?
True or false: Pinky Purple appears as a major color in our painting archive.

openers: Before the twentieth century, heather meant mottled, not purple.
